title: sre-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-12
content:
Quick on-call scratchpad - 2026-03-12
Owner: Lucas Morgan (SRE)
Collaborators: Sophia Wong, Noah Chen
Context: Night shift. Responsible for hosted-api EU region. Mostly steady but a brief incident around 02:10-03:30 UTC. Notes below are rough; will formalize into postmortem + runbook edits.

INCIDENT SUMMARY
- Time window: 2026-03-12 02:13 UTC -> 2026-03-12 03:02 UTC (partial recovery)
- Symptom: Spike in 5xx (503) for /v1/generate requests originating from eu-west routes. Client error rate ~18% for ~50m interval at peak.
- What paged: PagerDuty alert PD:SERVICE:HOSTED-API-eu-5xx-threshold
- Initial triage: Error pattern suggests upstream load-shedding on a small subset of GPU hosts (node-level OOM/eviction) -> cascading 503s when traffic routed there.

TIMELINE / ACTIONS
- 02:13 — PD page. I acked and joined the channel.
- 02:18 — Checked alert graphs (Console: per-route latency + token errors). Identified 3 hosts with elevated error rates and host-level GPU memory pressure.
- 02:22 — Rotated traffic away from affected AZ by updating smart-routing policy (temporary override) to prefer eu-west-1b/1c.
- 02:26 — SSH into node gpu-euw-07: rtnetlogs show repeated local allocator failures + driver messages. Restarted inference worker service on gpu-euw-07 (systemctl restart redwood-inference-worker).
- 02:31 — Node recovered, but two other hosts showing degraded perf. Coordinated with infra to cordon nodes and drain. K8s scale-up triggered to replace drained nodes.
- 02:50 — Error rate declined to baseline, but some requests still seeing elevated latency due to KV cache warmup.
- 03:02 — Restored normal routing. Monitored for 30m; no reoccurrence.

IMMEDIATE FOLLOW-UPS (high priority)
- F1: Runbook update: add diagnostic checklist for GPU host memory pressure + suggested restart steps and when to cordon. Owner: Sophia Wong. ETA: 2026-03-15. (Linked PR: runbooks/#58)
- F2: Alert tuning: reduce sensitivity of 5xx alert to transient spikes <5min or require sustained traffic-weighted error rate. Owner: Noah Chen. ETA: 2026-03-16. Jira: SRE-1423.
- F3: Add a pre-flight health check to smart-routing so traffic isn't sent to a host with recent allocator errors (lookup via host /healthz memory-pressure flag). Owner: Lucas Morgan. ETA: 2026-03-20.

POST-INCIDENT NOTES
- Root cause hypothesis: a set of hosts had a memory fragmentation pattern after a large batched job earlier in the evening; allocator failed to satisfy new requests leading to soft OOM, worker restarts, and 503s. Needs confirmation from infra (kernel logs + driver telemetry).
- KV cache warmup contributed to higher latency after recovery. Consider faster cache warming strategies for failover routing.

RUNBOOK TODOs (longer term)
- TODO 1: Add example commands for safe restart (systemctl restart + checking /var/log/redwood/inference.log for allocator errors).
- TODO 2: Document k8s node cordon/drain steps we actually executed and the signature of the autoscaler behavior (how many replacement nodes, cooldown).
- TODO 3: Add troubleshooting snippets for reading GPU driver logs and interpreting common allocator messages.
- TODO 4: Add a playbook section for verifying that KV cache warmup has completed (metrics to check: kv_hit_ratio, avg_token_latency)

NOTES / COMMANDS I RAN (for reference)
- k -n inference get pods -o wide | grep gpu-euw-0*
- ssh infra@gpu-euw-07 sudo journalctl -u redwood-inference-worker -n 200
- kubectl cordon gpu-node-23 && kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- curl -sS https://console.internal/redwood/metrics?range=1h&query=5xx_rate

MEASURED METRICS (quick)
- Peak error rate (5xx): ~18% at 02:20 UTC
- P95 latency during incident: 1.2s -> baseline 0.45s
- Approx number of affected requests: ~14k over 40m (estimate based on route traffic)

COMMUNICATIONS
- Notified CS triage at 02:35 UTC (brief message) — asked to hold external comms until we confirm extent.
- Draft postmortem placeholder created in Confluence: CONF-incident-2026-03-12 (update after root cause analysis).

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Was there a scheduled batch/maintenance that could have changed GPU memory fragmentation? (ask infra ops)
- Is our allocator telemetry sufficient to catch fragmentation patterns earlier?

NEXT STEPS (my personal todo)
- Today: create runbook PR with the restart checklist + add command snippets (finish by EOD 2026-03-12).
- This week: coordinate with infra to fetch full kernel/driver logs from affected hosts and confirm root cause (owner: Sophia).
- Follow-up meeting: schedule 30-minute debug session Monday 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC to review logs and finalize postmortem. Invite: infra, serving-runtime, SRE.

Quick reminders: keep notes terse in this doc and move finalized items to Confluence + link PRs/Jira.

-- Lucas
